Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-ai.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot kickoff / token volumes follow-up

Thanks for the call today, Marissa - good overview of Redwood's Dedicated options. A couple quick clarifications from our side to help with internal budgeting before we lock next steps:

- Expected monthly token volume: initial integration (NLP search + chat) looks like ~30M prompt tokens and ~70M completion tokens per month (so ~100M total). We expect growth to ~250M tokens/month within 3 months depending on feature rollout.
- Targeted unit economics we're looking at: ideally under $1,200 per 1M tokens (includes generation + embedding use across product).
- Procurement asked for a short usage/export so they can map to our SOW - can you share a sample usage CSV and a worked example of monthly cost at $/1M rates?

Also, the engineering team hit an early integration snag so we'll likely need an extra week on the pilot; curious if Redwood can extend the trial credits accordingly. Happy to share actual burn numbers if that helps.

Thanks,
Jordan
VP, Product
Acme.ai

Marissa / Dev - reviewed Jordan's numbers and the usage CSV. Quick internal notes and approval:

- Confirmed ask: Acme is seeing ~12M tokens/day now (~360M/month) but projects scale to ~250M/month. Current burn equates to ~360M/month if spike persists.
- Pricing: to hit Jordan's target (~$1,200 / 1M tokens) we recommend a combination: M2-quantized model variant for chat + aggressive prefix caching for embeddings-heavy flows. That gets close but we'll show 2 concrete scenarios in the sheet.

Credit extension decision: approved up to $10,000 in free pilot credits (applied to account) conditioned on:
1) a short mutual action plan (MAP) with clear success metrics and 30-day check-in, and
2) a one-page security/compliance sign-off from Acme (SOC2 questions already in flight).

Marissa - please apply the credit to deal ACME-2026-PILOT-42 and send Jordan the MAP and DocuSign link for the pilot amendment. Dev - can you stand by for a 30-min onboarding session tomorrow to review caching knobs?

Thanks,
